translations.text: I made this first account, O lover of God, about all that Jesus began to do and to teach,
until the day of his ascension, when he gave commands through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen, and was taken up;
to them he also presented himself alive after his passion in many ways. For forty days he appeared to them and spoke to them about the kingdom of God.
While he was staying with them, he commanded them: "Do not go away from Jerusalem, but wait for the promise of the Father, which you heard from me.
For John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit not many days after these."
Those who had gathered asked him, saying: "Lord, will you at this time restore the kingdom to Israel?"
He himself said to them: "It is not for you to know the times or the years, which the Father has set by his own authority;
but you will receive power at the coming of the Holy Spirit upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth."
When he had said this, while they were still watching, he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.
And as they were still standing and gazing at his ascension into heaven, behold, two men stood by them in white clothing,
who said to them: "Men of Galilee, why do you stand and look toward heaven? This Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same way as you saw him taken up into heaven."
Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mountain called the Mount of Olives, which is near Jerusalem, only about a Sabbath day's journey away.

And when they entered the city, they went up to the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John, James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot, and Judas son of James.
All of these were devoting themselves together to prayer, with the women, and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brothers.
In those days Peter stood up among the disciples and spoke (the crowd gathered together numbered about one hundred and twenty people):
"Men, it was necessary for this scripture to be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became the guide of those who seized Jesus,
for he was counted among us, and the portion of this ministry and apostleship had fallen to him by lot.
This man acquired that field with the wages of falsehood, and he swelled up and burst open in the middle, and all his bowels spilled out.
And it became known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, so that the field was even called in their own language Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.
For it is written in the Book of Psalms: 'Let his dwelling be desolate, and let there be no one living in it'; and 'Let another take his office.'
So it is necessary, of these men who have been gathered with us the whole time that the Lord Jesus came in and went out among us,
beginning from the baptism of John until the day he was taken up from us, that one of these become a witness of his resurrection with us."
And they put forward two: Joseph, who was called Barsabbas and was also named Justus, and Matthias.
And they prayed and said: "You, Lord, who know all hearts, show which one of these two
to receive the lot of the ministry, from which Judas went out to go to his own place."
And they cast lots for them. And the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was counted together with the eleven apostles as the twelfth.
And when that day of Pentecost was fulfilled, they were all together, gathered with one another,
and suddenly there came from heaven a roaring, like the rush of a violent wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting;
and there appeared to them divided tongues as of fire, and it rested upon each one of them.
And all were filled with the Holy Spirit, and they began to speak in foreign tongues, as the Spirit gave them to speak.
There were Jews dwelling in Jerusalem, God-fearing men from all the nations that are under heaven.
And when this sound came, the multitude of the people gathered and were confounded, because each one of them heard his own language when they spoke.
All were amazed and marvelled, and they said to one another: "Look, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
And how is it that we hear, each of us, our own language, we who are:
Persians and Uzhiks [?] and Elamites, and dwellers of Mesopotamia and of Judea and of Cappadocia, of Pontus and of Asia,
of Phrygia and of Pamphylia, of Egypt and of the parts of the region of Libya toward Cyrene, and visiting Romans,
Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabians: we hear them speaking in our own tongue these riches of God."
All were astonished, one with another, and they said: "What do these men mean to do?"
But others mocked them and said: "They are filled with sweet wine."
Peter stood among the eleven, raised his voice, and said to them: "Men of Judea, and all who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known among you, and give ear to my words,
for it is not as you suppose, that these men are drunk, for it is the third hour of this day.
But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel:

'And it shall come to pass after this, says the Lord God, that I will pour out of my Spirit upon all flesh, and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall see visions, and to your old men it shall be revealed in visions,
and upon my menservants and maidservants in those days of my Spirit, and they shall prophesy.
And I will give signs in the heavens and wonders upon the earth: blood and fire and vapour of smoke;
the sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood, before the coming of that great and appointed day of the Lord.
And it shall be that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.'
Men of Israel, hear my words. This Jesus of Nazareth, a man appointed by God for you with mighty works and signs and wonders, which God did through him among you, as you yourselves know,
this man, by the determined counsel and foreknowledge of God, and delivered up by the hands of lawless men, you nailed up and killed,
Whom God raised up, and loosed the pangs of death, because it was not possible for him to be held by it.
For David says concerning him: "I foresaw the Lord; he is always before me, for he is at my right hand, that I may not be shaken;
therefore my heart rejoiced, and my tongue rejoiced all the more; my flesh too shall dwell in hope.
For you will not leave my soul in hell, nor will you give your Holy One to see corruption;
you have made known to me, O Lord, your ways of life, and you will fill me with joy with your countenance."
Men, brothers, it is right to speak openly to you about the patriarch David: he died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this very day.
He was a prophet and knew that God had sworn to him with an oath that he would raise up the Christ from the fruit of his womb and seat him on his thrones.
He foretold and spoke of the resurrection of Christ, that his soul was not left in hell, nor did his flesh see corruption.
This Jesus God raised up, of which we are all witnesses.
He was exalted by the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Spirit from the Father, he poured out this which you see and hear.
For David did not ascend into heaven; he himself says: "The Lord said to my Lord: Sit at my right hand,
until I put your enemies beneath your feet."
Let all the house of Israel know clearly that God has made him Lord and Anointed, this Jesus whom you crucified."
When they heard this, they repented in their hearts and said to Peter and the other apostles: "What then shall we do, men, brothers?"
And Peter said to them: "Repent, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you will receive the promise of the Holy Spirit;
for the promise is yours and your children's and of all who are far off, whom the Lord our God calls."
And with many other words he testified to them, entreated them, and said to them: "Be saved from this crooked generation."
And they joyfully received his word, and on that day about three thousand were baptized.
And they were devoted to the teaching of the apostles and to fellowship and to blessing and to prayer.
Fear was upon every soul; many signs and wonders were done through the apostles in Jerusalem; great fear was upon them all.
All the believers were together and had everything in common;
they sold their estates and possessions and distributed them to all, as anyone had need.
Day by day they were devoted in the temple; they blessed bread from house to house and received their food with joyful and simple hearts;
they praised God and had favour with all the people.
And the Lord added more and more of the saved to the church day by day.
Peter and John were going up to the temple at the very hour of prayer, the ninth hour.

And there was a certain man who had been lame from his mother's womb. They would carry him and set him down day after day at the doors of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms of those going into the temple.
When he saw Peter and John as they were going into the temple, he asked them for alms.
Peter, together with John, looked at him and said to him: "Look at us."
And he looked at them, expecting to receive something from them.
Peter said to him: "We have no gold or silver; but what we have, we give to you: in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, arise and walk!"
And he took him by his right hand and raised him up. At once his feet and ankles were made strong;
and he stood up and walked, and went into the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
And all the people saw him walking and praising God.
They recognised him as the one who used to sit for alms at the Beautiful gates of the temple. And they were filled with fear and amazement at what had happened to him.
And as he held on to Peter and John, all the people gathered to them in the portico called Solomon's, because of the wonder.
When Peter saw this, he said to the people: "Men of Israel, why do you marvel at this? Or why do you look at us, as though we had made him walk by our own power or godliness?
The God of Abraham and the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified his son Jesus, whom you handed over and denied before Pilate, when he had decided to release him.
But you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a murderer instead.
And you killed the leader of life, whom God raised from the dead; of this we are witnesses.
And by faith in his name, his name has made strong this man whom you see and know; and the faith that comes through him has given him this life before all of you.
And now we know, brothers, that you acted in ignorance, as did your rulers.
But what God foretold by the mouth of all his prophets, the suffering of his anointed one, he has fulfilled in this way.
Now therefore repent and turn back, so that your sins may be wiped away,
so that, when the times of refreshing come from the presence of the Lord, he may send the one on whom you laid hands, Christ Jesus,
whom heaven must receive until the time of the restoration of all things, of which God spoke by the mouth of his holy prophets.
Moses said: "The Lord your God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; listen to him in everything he tells you.
And it shall be that every soul that does not listen to that prophet, that soul shall be cut off from his people."
And all the prophets from Samuel onward, one after another, as many as have spoken, have also foretold these days.
For you are the children of the prophets and of the covenant that God promised to your fathers, saying to Abraham: "Through your offspring all the families of the earth shall be blessed."
To you first he raised up his own Son Jesus and sent him to bless you, so that each one of you might turn from your wickedness."
And as they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
grieved because they were teaching the people and proclaiming through Jesus the resurrection of the dead.
And they laid their hands on them and put them in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.
And many of those who heard their word believed. And the number of the men who believed was about five thousand.
And on the next day their rulers, elders and scribes gathered in Jerusalem,
with Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander and all who were of the high priests' family.
And they set them in their midst and asked them: "By what power or by what name have you done this?"
Then Peter was filled with the Holy Spirit and said to them: "Rulers of the people and elders of Israel,
if we are being examined today about a good deed done to a sick man, by which he has been saved,

let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that it is by the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead: through him this man stands before you alive.
This is the stone which was despised by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner. And there is no salvation from anyone else,
nor is there any other name under heaven given to men by which we must be saved."
Now they saw the boldness of Peter and of John, and they knew that they were unlettered, ignorant men. They marvelled, and they recognised that they had been with Jesus.
And they saw the man who had been healed standing with them, and they could not dispute it.
And they ordered them to go outside the council. They spoke with one another
and said: "What are we to do with these men? For a sign has been made manifest through them among all the inhabitants of Jerusalem [?], and we cannot deny it.
But so that it may not spread further among the people, let us threaten them not to speak to anyone in this name."
And they called them and commanded them: "Do not speak at all, and do not teach in the name of Jesus."
But Peter and John answered and said to them: "Whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge.
For we cannot help speaking of what we have seen and heard."
But they threatened them further over this and released them. They could find no way to punish them, because of the people, for everyone was glorifying God for what had happened.
For the man on whom this sign of healing had been done was more than forty years old.
And when they had been released, they went to their own people and told them what the high priests and the elders had said to them.
And when they heard this, they raised their voice together to God and said: "Lord, you are God, who made heaven and earth and everything that is in it,
who through our father, by the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of your servant David, said: "Why did the nations rage, and the people plot vain things?
The kings of the earth came, and the rulers gathered together against the Lord and against his Anointed."
For truly in this holy city they gathered together against your holy Son Jesus, whom you anointed: Herod and Pontius Pilate, with the Gentiles, together with the people of Israel,
to do whatever your hand and your counsel had determined beforehand should happen.
And now, Lord, look upon their words, and grant your servants to speak your word with all boldness,
while you stretch out your hand to heal and to do signs and wonders through the name of your holy Son Jesus."
And at their prayer the place where they were gathered was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God boldly.
And the multitude of those who believed were of one heart and one mind, and not one of them said that his possessions were his own, but they held everything in common.
And with great power the apostles bore witness to the resurrection of our Lord Jesus Christ, and great grace was upon them all.
No one among them was in need, and those who owned fields or houses sold them and brought the price of what they sold,
and laid it at the feet of the apostles, and it was given to each person according to what each one needed.
And Joseph, whom the apostles called Barnabas, meaning son of consolation, a Levite and a Cypriot by birth,
sold [it], brought the price, and laid it at the feet of the apostles.
A certain man named Ananias, with his wife Sapphira, sold a field
and kept back part of the price (his wife also knew of this), and he brought only a part and laid it at the feet of the apostles.
Peter said to him: "Ananias, why has the devil filled your heart, so that you lied to the Holy Spirit and kept back part of the price of the field?
While it remained unsold, was it not yours? And after you sold it, was it not still in your power? Why have you set this deed in your heart? You did not lie to men but to God."
When Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last. And great fear fell on all who heard of this.
The young men got up, wrapped him, carried him out, and buried him.
After an interval of about three hours, his wife came in, not knowing what had happened.
Peter said to her: "Tell me, did you sell the field for this much?" And she said: "Yes, for that much."
Peter said to her: "Why have you agreed together like this to test the Holy Spirit? Look, are not the feet of those who buried your husband standing at the door, and they will carry you out as well?"
At once she fell at his feet and breathed her last. The young men came in, found her dead, carried her out, and buried her beside her husband.
And great fear came upon the whole congregation and upon all who heard of this.
And many signs were done among the people by the hands of the apostles, and they were all together in Solomon's portico.
But the others could not touch them, yet the people held them in high honour.
And all the more a multitude of men and women who believed in the Lord was added,
so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on beds and stretchers, so that when Peter came by, at least his shadow might fall on some of them.
And a multitude from the cities around gathered to Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those troubled by unclean spirits, and they were all healed.
The high priest rose up, and all who were with him, that is, the sect of the Sadducees, and they were filled with jealousy,
and they laid their hands on the apostles and put them in the public prison to be kept there.
But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, brought them out, and said:
"Go, stand in the temple, and speak to the people all the words of this life."

When they heard this, they went into the temple at daybreak and taught the people. Then the high priest and those with him came and called together the council and all the elders of the sons of Israel, and they sent to the prison to have the apostles brought.
But when the servants went there, they did not find them in the prison. They came back and told them:
"We found the prison locked with every security, and the guards standing in front of the doors. But when we opened them, we found no one inside."
When the captain of the temple and the high priests heard these words, they were puzzled about them and wondered what this could be.
Then someone came and told them: "The men whom you put in prison are in the temple, standing and teaching the people."
Then the captain went with the servants and brought them, but not by force, because he was afraid that the people might stone them.
He brought them and stood them in the middle of the council. The high priest questioned them
and said: "Did we not strictly command you not to teach in that name? And now, look, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you would bring this man's blood upon us."
Peter and the apostles answered and said: "We must obey God rather than men.
The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, on whom you laid hands and whom you hung on a tree.
God exalted him with his right hand as Leader and Saviour, to give repentance to Israel and forgiveness of sins.
And we are his witnesses to these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey him."
When they heard this, they were cut to the heart and planned to kill them.
But a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law who was honoured among the people, stood up in the council and ordered that the men be put outside.
And he said to them: "Men of Israel, be careful about what you intend to do to these men.
For some time ago Theudas rose up, claiming to be somebody, and about four hundred men followed him. He too was destroyed, and all who followed him were scattered and came to nothing.
After him, Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew many people after him. He too perished, and all who followed him were dispersed.
"And now I tell you, keep away from these men and let them go. If this word or this deed is from men, it will be overthrown;
but if it is from God, you will not be able to overthrow them, lest you even be found fighting against God." And they obeyed him.
And they summoned the apostles, beat them, and commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
And they departed from the council rejoicing, because they had been found worthy to be dishonoured for his name.
And every day they were in the temple, and they did not cease teaching and preaching the gospel of Jesus Christ.
In those days, as the disciples were multiplying, there arose a murmuring of the Greeks against the Hebrews, because their widows were being neglected in the daily ministration.
Then the Twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said to them: "It is not pleasing to us to leave the word of God and serve tables.
Choose, brothers, seven men from among you who are well attested, full of the Holy Spirit and of wisdom, whom we may appoint over this need.
But we will devote ourselves to prayer and to the ministry of this word."

And the word seemed pleasing before the whole multitude, and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, and Prochorus, and Nicanor, and Timon, and Parmenas, and Nicolaus, a proselyte of Antioch.
And they prayed and laid their hands on them.
And the word of the Lord grew, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem multiplied greatly in the faith.
And Stephen was full of the Holy Spirit and of power, and he worked signs and wonders among the great multitude of the people.
Then some men rose up from the synagogue called that of the Libertines (Freedmen), and from Cilicia and from Asia, and of the Cyrenians and of the Alexandrians, and they disputed with Stephen,
and they could not withstand the wisdom and the Holy Spirit with which he spoke.
Then they secretly induced some men, who said: "We heard him speaking words of blasphemy against Moses and against God."
They stirred up the people and the elders and the scribes, and they came upon him, seized him, and brought him before the council.
And they set up false witnesses, who said: "This man does not cease speaking evil words against this holy place and the law;
for we heard him say that Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the law which Moses gave us."
And all who sat there in the council looked at him and saw his face like the face of an angel.
The high priest said to him: "Are these things so?"
And he said: "Men, brothers and fathers, hear me. The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he settled in Haran,
and said to him: 'Go out from your land and from your kindred to the land which I will show you.'
Then he went out from the land of the Chaldeans and dwelt in Haran. Then, after the death of his father, he came to this land in which you now dwell.
And he gave him no inheritance in it, not even a place to set his foot, but he promised to give it to him as a possession, and to his offspring, though he had no child.
God said to him: "Your offspring will be sojourners in a foreign land, and they will enslave them and do evil to them for four hundred years."
"And I will judge the nation that they serve," said the Lord, "and after this they will come out and serve me in this place."
And he gave him the law of circumcision. And he became the father of Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob of the twelve patriarchs.
And the patriarchs were jealous of Joseph and sold him into Egypt, and God was with him,
and he rescued him from all his afflictions and gave him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of the Egyptians. And he made him ruler over Egypt and over all his house.
There was a famine in Egypt and in Canaan, and great affliction. And our fathers could not find food.
When Jacob heard that there was food in Egypt, he sent our fathers the first time,
and on the second visit Joseph made himself known to his brothers, and Joseph's family became known to Pharaoh's house;
Joseph sent and called for Jacob his father and all his kindred, seventy-five souls.
And Jacob went down to Egypt, and he died, he and our fathers.
And they were carried to Shechem and buried in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
And as the time of the promise that God had promised to Abraham drew near, the people grew and multiplied in Egypt,
until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
He oppressed our people and did evil to our fathers, and made them cast out their infants so that they would not live.
At that time Moses was born, and he was beautiful before God. He was brought up for three months in his father's house.
And when they had cast him out, Pharaoh's daughter took him up and brought him up as her own son.
And Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians; he was mighty in words and deeds.
And when forty years of his life were being completed, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the sons of Israel,
and he saw someone being wronged; he set upon the one doing the harm, took vengeance on behalf of the wronged man, and killed the Egyptian.
He supposed that his brothers would understand that God was giving them salvation by his hand, but they did not understand.
On the next day he appeared to them as they were quarreling, and he tried to reconcile them in peace, and said to them: "Men, you are brothers; why do you wrong one another?"
But the one who was wronging his neighbor pushed him away and said: "Who made you ruler and judge over us?
Or do you want to kill me, as you killed the Egyptian yesterday?"
And at this word Moses fled, and he lived as a sojourner in the land of Midian, where two sons were born to him.
And when forty years had been completed, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai in a flame of fire in a bush;
Moses was amazed when he saw the vision, and as he went up to look at it, the voice of the Lord came:
"I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac and the God of Jacob." Moses trembled and did not dare to look.
The Lord said to him: "Take the sandals off your feet, for the place where you are standing is holy ground.
I have truly seen the affliction of my people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to rescue them. Now come, I will send you to Egypt."
This Moses they had rejected, saying, "Who made you ruler and judge over us?" Yet God sent this man as ruler and deliverer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
He led them out, and he did wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, at the Red Sea and in the wilderness for forty years.
This is the Moses who said to the children of Israel: "The Lord God will raise up for you a prophet from among your brothers, like me; listen to him."
This is the one who was with the people in the wilderness, with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai, and with our fathers. He received living words to give to you.
Your fathers refused to obey him. Instead they pushed him away, and in their hearts they turned back to the land of Egypt.
They said to Aaron: "Make us gods who will go before us. As for Moses, who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him."
In those days they set up the calf, offered sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the work of their hands.

God turned away and gave them over to serve the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the prophets: "Did you offer me slain beasts and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
You took up the tent of Moloch and the star of your god Rephan, the idols that you made in order to worship them. So I will remove you beyond Babylon."
Our fathers had the tent of witness with them in the wilderness. It was made as the one who spoke to Moses commanded: he was to make it according to the pattern he had seen.

Our fathers received it in turn and brought it in with Joshua when they took possession of the land of the nations. God drove those nations out before our fathers. So it remained until the days of David,
who found favor before God and asked to find a dwelling place for the God of Jacob.
But it was Solomon who built him a house.
But the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet said:
"Heaven is my throne, and the earth is the footstool of my feet. What kind of house will you build for me, says the Lord, or what place could be my place of rest?
Did not my hand make all these things?"
You hard-hearted and stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in heart and ears! You always rise up against the Holy Spirit to oppose him. As your fathers did, so do you.
Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? They killed those who foretold the coming of the Holy One, and now you have become his betrayers and murderers,
You received the law by the command of angels and did not keep it."
When they heard this, they were cut to the heart and gnashed their teeth at him.
But he, full of faith and the Holy Spirit, looked up to heaven and saw the glory of the Lord, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God.
And he said: "Behold, I see the heavens opened and the Son of God standing at the right hand of God."
They cried out with a loud voice, covered their ears with their hands, and rushed upon him,
and they took him outside the city and stoned him. And those who were killing him took off their garments and laid them at the feet of a certain young man whose name was Saul.
And they stoned Stephen, and he cried out and said: "Lord, receive my spirit."
He knelt down, cried out, and said with a loud voice: "Lord, do not hold this sin against them." And when he had said this, he fell asleep.

This Saul approved of his killing. In those days there was a great persecution against the church that was in Jerusalem, and all were scattered here and there [?] through the countryside of Judea, except the apostles.
God-fearing men came and took up Stephen, and they made great lamentation over him.
This Saul was doing great harm to the churches. He entered houses, dragged off men and women (literally "fathers and mothers"), and handed them over to prison.
The apostles went about from place to place and proclaimed the word of life.
Philip went down to the city of the Samaritans and preached Christ to them.
The people paid attention to the words he spoke to them, all of them together hearing him and seeing the signs that he performed.
For from those who had unclean spirits, the spirits would cry out with a loud voice and come out. And many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
And there was great joy in that city.

There was a certain man named Simon, who had been in that city for some time before. He practiced sorcery and astonished the people of the Samaritans, and he said of himself that he was someone great.
All of them, from the least to the greatest, paid attention to him and said: "This man is the power of God that is called Great."
They listened to him, because for a long time he had amazed them with his sorcery.
And when they believed Philip's good news about the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
And Simon himself also believed and was baptized, and he was astonished and followed Philip. As he saw the signs and the very great miracles that were being done, he was amazed.
Now when the apostles who were in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them.
When they arrived, they prayed for them, that the Holy Spirit might come upon them.
For until then the Holy Spirit had not yet come upon any of them; they had only been baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
Then they laid their hands on them, and the Holy Spirit came upon them.
When Simon saw that the Holy Spirit was given through the laying on of the apostles' hands, he offered them money
and said, "Give me this power too, so that anyone on whom I lay my hand may receive the Holy Spirit."
Peter said to him, "May your silver perish with you, because you thought you could obtain the gift of God with money.
You have no part or inheritance in this matter, for your heart is not upright before God.
So repent now of your wickedness and pray to the Lord, in the hope that this wickedness of the thoughts of your heart may be forgiven you.
For I see that you are in the bitterness of gall and bound up in sin, for so you are."
Simon answered and said, "Pray to the Lord for me, so that none of what you have said may come upon me."
They spread abroad the testimony of the word and spoke the word of the Lord, and they returned to Jerusalem, preaching the gospel in many other villages and towns of the Samaritans as well.
An angel of the Lord spoke to Philip and said, "Get up and go south, to the road that goes down from Jerusalem to Gaza. It is a desert."
Philip got up at once and went. And behold, there was an Indian, a eunuch, a powerful official of Candace, queen of India, who was in charge of all her treasure. He had gone to Jerusalem to worship.
He was returning, sitting in his chariot and reading the prophet Isaiah.
The Holy Spirit said to Philip, "Go over and approach that chariot."
So Philip went over and began to listen as he read the prophet Isaiah. He began to question him and said, "Do you understand what you are reading?"
He answered and said, "How can I understand unless someone guides me?" And he begged Philip to come up and sit with him in the chariot.
The passage of Scripture he was reading was this: "Like a sheep he was given over to slaughter, and like a lamb stands silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth.
In his humiliation his justice was taken away from him. Who will search out his lineage? For his life is taken away from the earth."
The eunuch answered Philip and said, "I beg you, about whom does the prophet say this? About himself, or about someone else?"
Philip opened his mouth and, starting from these scriptures, began to proclaim the good news of Jesus to him.
As they were going along the road, they came to some water, and the eunuch said, "Look, here is water. What now prevents me from being baptized?"
Philip said to him, "If you believe with all your heart, it is permitted." He answered and said to him, "I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God."
He ordered the chariot to stop, and both of them, Philip and the eunuch, went down into the water, and he baptized him.
And when they came up out of the water, the Holy Spirit came upon the eunuch. And the angel of the Lord snatched Philip away, and the eunuch saw him no more, and he went on his way with joy.
And Philip was found in the region of Azotus; there he went about and preached the gospel to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
And Saul raged all the more and was full of anger and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord; he went to the high priest
and asked him for letters to Damascus, to the other synagogues, so that he might go and, if he found any who were of the way of this teaching, men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
And as he was going along and drew near to Damascus, suddenly a brightness of light from heaven shone around him.
And he fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to him: "Saul, Saul, why do you persecute me? It is hard for you to kick against the goad."
He answered and said to him: "Who are you, Lord?" He said to him: "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
But rise and go into the city, and there you will be told what it is fitting for you to do."
And the men who were with him stood amazed; they heard the voice, but they saw no one.
Saul rose from the ground; his eyes were open, yet he saw nothing. Those with him took him by the hand and led him into Damascus.
And three days passed, and he saw nothing, and neither ate nor drank.
There was a man there, one of the disciples, whose name was Ananias. And the Lord said to him in a vision: "Ananias!" And he said: "Here I am, Lord."
The Lord said to him: "Rise quickly and go to the quarter that is called Straight Street, and look in the house of Judas for Saul, who is called the man of Tarsus,
for behold, he is praying there." And he had seen in a vision a man named Ananias come in and lay his hands on him, so that he might regain his sight.
Ananias answered and said: "Lord, I have heard from many about this man, how much evil he has done to your saints in Jerusalem,
and now he has come here too for this purpose, and has received authority from the high priests to lead away in bonds all who call on your name."
The Lord said to him: "Go, for I am with you; I have found him a chosen vessel, to bear my name before all the Gentiles, kings and rulers, and the sons of Israel.
And I will show him how much suffering he must take upon himself for the sake of my name."

Ananias rose at once and went, and came and entered the house, and laid his hands on him and said: "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me to you, Jesus, who appeared to you on the road by which you were coming, so that you may regain the sight of your eyes and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he began to see, and he rose and was baptized;
and he took food and was strengthened.
And he was there with the disciples in Damascus for some days, and he immediately began to preach in the synagogues and to say: "This is Jesus, the Son of God."

All who heard him were amazed and said, "Is this not the man who was destroying those in Jerusalem who called on the name of Jesus? And he came here for that very purpose, to bind any he found following this Way and take them to the chief priests in Jerusalem."
But Saul grew stronger and stronger. He gathered all the Jews who lived in Damascus, taught the people, and declared that this is the Christ.
When many days had passed, the Jews plotted to kill him.
Someone revealed this to Saul: they were watching the gates of the city night and day so that they might kill [?] him.
The brothers took him and let him down through a window in the wall in a basket.
He went to Jerusalem, and afterwards he tried to join the disciples. But they were all afraid of him; they did not believe that he was a disciple.

Barnabas took him, brought him to the apostles, and told them how he had seen the Lord on the road and that the Lord had spoken to him, and how in Damascus his name had been made known [?] by the name of Jesus.
He stayed with them, going in and out in Jerusalem, and spoke openly in the name of the Lord.
He spoke and debated with the Greek-speakers, and they were plotting to kill him.
When the brothers learned of this, they took him to Caesarea and sent him off to Tarsus.

The churches in all the regions of Judea, Galilee and Samaria were at peace, being built up and strengthened. They walked in the fear of the Lord and grew strong through the comfort of the Holy Spirit.
As Peter was travelling through all those regions, he came down also to the saints who lived in Lydda.
There he found a man named Aeneas who had been sick for eight years, lying bedridden on his bed, for he was paralysed.
Peter said to him, "Aeneas, the Lord Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed."
At once he got up and stood upright. All the inhabitants of Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
In Joppa there was a woman disciple named Tabitha, which translated means Dorcas ("gazelle"). She was full of good works and of the acts of charity that she did.
In those days she fell sick and died. They washed the body, clothed it, carried it up, and laid it in the upper room.
Since Lydda is near Joppa, the disciples heard that Peter was there. They sent two men to him and told him, "Do not hesitate to come to us at once."

Peter got up at once and went with them. When they arrived, they led him and took him up to the upper room. All the widows stood around him, weeping and showing him the tunics and all the clothing that Tabitha had made while she was with them.

He had the whole crowd put outside. Peter knelt down and prayed, then turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, arise in the name of Jesus Christ." At once she opened her eyes. When she saw Peter, she sat up.
He gave her his hand and raised her up. He called the saints, the widows, and presented her to them alive.
This became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
He stayed there in Joppa for many days, with a certain man, Simon the tanner.
And there was a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the band called the Italian,
devout and fearing the Lord, with all his household. He gave many alms among the people and prayed to God always.
He clearly saw a vision at about the ninth hour of the day: an angel of the Lord came to him and said to him, "Cornelius!"
And he looked at him, was seized with terror out of fear, and said, "Who are you, lord?" He said to him, "Your prayers and your alms have gone up before the Lord as a memorial for you.
And now send men to Joppa and bring Simon, who is called Peter.
His lodging is with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is beside the sea."
When the angel who had spoken to him had gone, he called two of his servants and a devout soldier, one of those who always attended him,
and he told them all this and sent them to Joppa.
And the next day, as they were on their way and drawing near the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray at about the ninth hour.
He became hungry and wanted to eat. And while they were preparing food for him, a trance came over him,
and he saw the heavens opened, and a vessel like a great linen sheet, by its four corners, from heaven to earth;
and in it were all the four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth and the birds of the sky.
And a voice came to Peter and said, "Get up, Peter, kill and eat."
Peter answered and said, "Certainly not, Lord, for nothing defiled and unclean has ever entered my mouth."
Then the voice came a second time and said to him, "What God has made clean, you must not regard as defiled."
This happened three times, and the vessel was taken back up into heaven.
While Peter was pondering in his heart what the vision shown to him might mean, behold, the men who had come from Cornelius were asking for Simon's house, and they came and stood at his gate.
They called someone out and asked, "Is this really the lodging of Simon, who is called Peter?"
And while Peter stood pondering the vision, the Holy Spirit said to him, "Behold, three men are standing outside looking for you;
get up, go down, and go with them, and do not doubt at all, for I have sent them to you."
Peter got up at once, went down to the men, and said, "Here I am, the one you are looking for. Now, what is the matter for which you have come?"

They answered and said to him, "Cornelius the centurion, a righteous and God-fearing man who is well spoken of by the whole nation of the Jews, received a command from an angel to bring you to his house and to hear words from you."
He invited the men in and kept them there that day. The next day he got up and went with them, and some of the brothers who were in Joppa went with him.
And the next day they entered Caesarea. Cornelius was waiting for him and had gathered his relatives and close friends.
And when Peter came in, Cornelius came to meet him, fell at his feet and worshipped him.
Peter raised him up and said to him: "Stand up, for I myself am also only a man."
And they talked together, and so they went inside, and he found a large gathering there.

Peter said to them: "You yourselves know that it is in no way proper for a Jewish man to associate with gentiles or to touch those of a foreign race. But God has given me a command that I should in no way regard any man as defiled or unclean.
Therefore I came to you without objecting. Now I wish to know for what matter you summoned me."

And Cornelius said to him: "Four days ago, at this very hour, I was praying in my worship at the ninth hour in this house of mine. A man in shining white clothing came and stood before me and said to me:
'Cornelius, your prayers and the alms of your good works have gone up as a memorial for you before God.
Now send to Joppa and summon Simon, who is called Peter. He is lodging at the house of a certain Simon, a tanner, by the seashore. He will come and speak to you.'
Because of this I sent for you at once, and you have done well to come. Now, behold, we are all present before God to hear everything that the Lord has commanded you."
Peter opened his mouth and said: "I truly know this, that there is no partiality with God,
but in every nation whoever fears him and does righteousness is acceptable to him.
The word which he sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace through Jesus Christ: he himself is Lord of all.
You yourselves know the word that went throughout all Judea, which began from Galilee after the baptism that John preached:

Jesus of Nazareth, whom the Lord anointed with the Holy Spirit and with power, who came and went about among us doing good works and healing the sick, and freeing those who were oppressed by the devil, for God was with him.
And we are witnesses of all the deeds that he did in the land of Judea and in the city of Jerusalem. Him they killed by hanging him on the tree;
him God raised up on the third day and allowed him to be seen openly,
not by all the people, but by the disciples chosen beforehand by God, that is, by us, who ate and drank with him after his resurrection from the dead.
And he commanded us to preach to the people and to testify that he himself is the one chosen by God as judge of the living and the dead.
To all this all the prophets bear witness, that all who believe in him receive forgiveness of sins through his name."
While Peter was still saying this, the Holy Spirit came and rested upon all who were hearing the word.
The believers from among the circumcised who had come in with Peter were amazed that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the gentiles as well,
for they heard them speaking in various tongues and glorifying God.

At that time Peter answered and said: "Let there be no hindrance from water to the baptism of these people, who are already filled with the Holy Spirit just as we are, we who have believed this from the beginning."
And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ. Then they begged him to stay with them for some days.
The apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out on the Gentiles as well.
But when Peter came to Jerusalem, the brothers who were of the circumcision kept away from him,
because he had gone in among uncircumcised men and eaten with them.
Then Peter began to tell them everything from the beginning, and said:

"I was in the city of Joppa, and while I was at worship I saw an astonishing vision: a kind of vessel was coming down, like a great linen sheet, hanging from heaven by its four corners. It came down and reached right to me.
As I looked at it, I saw every kind of four-footed animal, the wild beasts of the earth, the creeping things of the earth and the birds of the sky.
And I heard the voice saying to me: 'Get up, Peter, kill and eat.'
And I said: 'Far be it from me, Lord, for nothing defiled or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
A voice came from heaven and said: 'What God has made clean, you must not consider defiled.'
And at that very moment three men arrived at the gates of the house where I was staying. They had been sent to me from Caesarea.
The Holy Spirit said to me: 'Get up and go with them without doubting.' These brothers also came with me, and we went into the man's house.
He began to tell us how he had seen an angel standing in his house, who said to him: 'Send to Joppa and bring Simon, who is called Peter,
who will speak a word to you by which you and all your household will be saved.'
And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit came upon them, as it came upon us at first,
and I remembered the word of the Lord, when he said: 'John baptized with water, but you will be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
So if God gave the Gentiles the same grace that he first gave us, who have believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, what power did I have to hinder God?"
When they heard this, they fell silent and glorified God, saying: "So God has seen fit to grant the Gentiles also the repentance that leads to life."

The apostles were scattered by the persecution that arose over Stephen. Some of them went along the seacoast, and some went to Cyprus and Antioch. They spoke the word to no outsider, but only to the Jews.
Some of them were men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who came to Antioch and spoke to the Greek-speakers, preaching the good news of the Lord Jesus.
And the hand of the Lord was with them to heal people, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
News of them reached the ears of the people in Jerusalem, and they sent Barnabas as far as Antioch.
When he came and saw the grace of God, he rejoiced, and he urged them all to remain with the Lord with earnest hearts,
for he was a good man, full of the Holy Spirit and of faith. And many people were added to the Lord.
Then he went out to Tarsus to look for Saul. He found him and brought him back, and they came to Antioch.
They were there for a whole year, gathering the church and teaching that great multitude. And it was in Antioch that the disciples were first called Christians.
In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
One of them, whose name was Agabus, stood up and announced by the Holy Spirit that a severe famine was going to come over the whole world. This happened in the days of Claudius Caesar.
So the disciples decided that each of them, as far as he was able, would send relief to the brethren who lived in Judea.
They did this, and sent it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas.
At that very time King Herod laid hands on some members of the church to harm them.
He killed James, the brother of John, with the sword.
When he saw that this pleased the Jews, he went further and arrested Peter as well. These were the days of Unleavened Bread.

He seized him, put him in prison, and handed him over to four squads of four soldiers each to guard him. He intended to bring him out after the days of Passover, so that they would hand him over into the hands of the people.
So Peter was kept in the prison, but the churches were praying earnestly to God for him.

When Herod was about to bring him out and hand him over into their hands, on that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with double chains, while the prison guards in front of the doors were guarding the prison.

Then an angel of the Lord came, and a great light shone in the building. He struck Peter on the side, woke him, and said to him: "Get up quickly." And at once the chains came loose and fell from his hands.
The angel said to him: "Put on your belt and fasten on your sandals." And he did so. Then he said: "Put on your garment and follow me."
He went out and followed him. He did not know that what the angel was doing was real; he thought he was seeing a vision.

When they had passed the first and the second guard, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, and it opened for them by itself. When they had gone through, they passed along one street, and immediately the angel left him.
When Peter came to himself, he said in his mind: "Now I know truly that God has sent his angel and rescued me from the hands of Herod and from all that the Jewish people were expecting."
Having thought this over, he went to the house of Mary, the mother of John who was called Mark, where many people were gathered and praying.
When he knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came out to answer.
When she recognized Peter's voice, in her joy she did not open the door, but ran inside and told them: "Look, Peter is standing at the door."
They said to her: "You must be out of your mind." But she kept insisting all the more: "It is so." And they said: "It must be his angel."
Meanwhile Peter kept knocking at the door. When they opened it and saw him, they were amazed.

Then he motioned to them with his hand to be silent. Then he told them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison, and he instructed them: "Tell this to James and the brethren." And he went away to another place.
And when day dawned, there was no small commotion among the soldiers over this: "Where has Peter gone?"
Herod searched for him and did not find him. Then he interrogated the guards and ordered them to be put to death. And Herod went out from there, from Judea, and stayed at Caesarea.

And Herod was furious with the people of Tyre and Sidon. They had come to him together, and they made Aristacus [?], the king's chamberlain, their benefactor and asked for peace, because their country was fed from the king's country.
On a certain appointed day Herod put on royal robes, sat on the throne, and spoke to them.
And all the people cried out with one voice, saying: "This is the voice of God and not of men."
At once an angel of the Lord struck him down, because he did not give the glory to God, and he became food for worms and breathed his last.
And the word of God grew and multiplied.
Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem to Antioch when they had completed their ministry, and they took with them John, who was also called Mark.

And in Antioch, in the church that was there, there were certain prophets and teachers: Barnabas; Simeon, who was called Niger; Lucius of Cyrene; Manaen, who was the foster-brother of King Herod; and Saul.
While they were standing in the service of the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said: "Choose out for me and set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."
Then they prayed and fasted, laid their hands on them, and sent them off.
When they had been sent out from there, led by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia. From there they boarded a ship and set sail for Cyprus.
And from there they went on [?] to Salamis and began to proclaim the word of God in the synagogue of the Jews. They also had John with them as their assistant.
When they had gone through all the cities as far as Paphos, they found there a certain man, a magician, a false prophet, a Jew, whose name was Bar-Jesus.
He was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The proconsul summoned Barnabas and Saul and sought to hear the word of God from them.
But Elymas the magician (for that is how his name is translated) opposed them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the miracles.
But Saul, who is Paul, was filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him
and said: "O you who are full of all deceit and wickedness, offspring of the devil and enemy of all righteousness, will you not stop perverting the straight ways of the Lord?

And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you will be blind and will not see the sun for a time." Immediately mist and darkness fell upon him, and he went about seeking someone to lead him.
Then, when the proconsul saw what had happened, he believed and was astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
Paul and his companions departed from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia. But John separated from them and went back from there to Jerusalem.
They went on from Perga to Antioch of Pisidia. When they came to the synagogue on the Sabbath day, they sat down.
After the Law and the Prophets had been read, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them and said to those men, "Men, brothers, if you have any words of encouragement for this people, speak."
Paul stood up and raised his hand for them to be silent, and said: "Men of Israel, and those among you who fear God, listen to me.
The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and made the people great during their stay as strangers in the land of Egypt. With an uplifted arm he brought them out of it,
and for about forty years he fed them in the wilderness.
He destroyed seven nations in the land of Canaan and gave them that land of theirs as an inheritance,
for about four hundred and fifty years. After this he gave them judges until the days of Samuel the prophet.
Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for about forty years.

When he had removed him, he raised up David to be their king. God himself testified about him and said, 'I have found David son of Jesse, a man after my own heart, who will do and carry out all the will of my heart.'
From this man's descendants God, as he had promised, raised up for Israel the Savior, Jesus,
before whose coming John the Baptist had first preached a baptism of repentance to all Israel.
As John was finishing his course, he said, 'Who do you think I am? I am not he. But look, one is coming after me, and I am not worthy to untie the straps of his sandals.'
Men, brothers, children of the family of Abraham, and those among you who fear God: the word of this salvation has been sent to you.
For the people who live in Jerusalem and their rulers did not recognize him. By condemning him they fulfilled the words of the prophets that are read every Sabbath.
They found no reason for putting him to death, and yet they asked Pilate to have him killed.
When they had carried out everything that was written about him, they took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead,
and for many days he appeared to those who had come up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to the people.
And we bring you the good news of the gift that was promised to your fathers:
God has fulfilled this for their children, for us, by raising up Jesus. As it is written in the second psalm: 'You are my Son; today I have begotten you.'
And about raising him from the dead, never again to return to decay, he said this: 'I will give you the holy and sure blessings of David.'
So he also says in another place: 'You will not let your Holy One see decay.'
For David served in his own generation and by the will of God fell asleep. He was laid with his fathers and saw decay.
But the one whom God raised did not see decay.
Let this be known to you, men, brothers: through him the forgiveness of your sins is proclaimed to you, and from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses,
by him everyone who believes is justified.
Take care, then, that the word spoken by the prophet does not come upon you:
"Look, you despisers, and be amazed, and perish, for I am doing a work in your days, a work that you will not believe even if someone tells it to you."
And as they were about to leave, the people begged them to speak that word of God to them on the next Sabbath as well.
When they had dismissed the assembly, many of the Jews and of the believing proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, for they strengthened them and urged them to stand firm in the grace of God.
On the next Sabbath the whole city gathered to hear the word of the Lord.
When the Jews saw so great a crowd, they were filled with envy, rose up to contradict the words spoken by Paul, and reviled them.

Barnabas and Paul spoke out boldly and said: "It was necessary that this word of God be spoken to you first. Since you, as you see, push it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, behold, we are turning to the Gentiles.
For this is what the Lord commanded us: 'I have set you as a light for the Gentiles, so that you may be for salvation to the ends of the earth.'"
When the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord. And as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.
And the word of the Lord spread throughout all that region.

But the Jews stirred up the devout women of rank and the leading men of that city, and raised a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and drove them out of the city and expelled them from their territory.
But they shook off the dust of their feet against them and went to the city of Iconium.
And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
In Iconium it happened that, according to custom, we went into the synagogue of the Jews and spoke in such a way that a great multitude of Jews and Gentiles believed.
But the Jews who did not believe stirred up the hearts of the Gentiles and turned them bitter against the brothers.
For a long time they carried on, speaking boldly for the Lord, who bore witness to the words of his grace and granted signs and wonders to be done by their hands.
Then the people of that city were divided: some were with the Jews and some with the apostles.
And when the Jews and the Gentiles, together with their rulers, conspired to go against them, insult them and stone them,
they left that place and fled, and took refuge in the cities of Lycaonia, Lystra and Derbe, and in the surrounding villages,
and there they preached the gospel.
And there was a man there, in Lystra, who was weak in his feet and lame from his mother's womb. He sat there and had never walked.
He heard the words that Paul was speaking. When Paul looked at him and saw that he had faith to be saved, he said to him in a loud voice:
"I tell you, man, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ: stand up straight on your feet." He sprang up and began to walk.
When the crowd saw what Paul had done, they raised their voice in the Lycaonian tongue and said: "The idols have become like men and have come down to us."
And they called Barnabas the idol Zeus, and Paul Hermes, because Paul was the leader in speaking.
And the priest of the idol of Zeus, for he belonged to the ruler of that city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates of the city with the crowd, and wished to offer sacrifice.
When the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard this, they tore their clothes and rushed down to the crowd, crying out

and saying: "Men, why are you doing this? For we too are men like you, and we bring you good news, that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made heaven and earth, the sea and everything that is in it;
who in the generations that have passed allowed all the nations to walk in the ways of their own will;
and yet he did not at any time leave his beneficence without witness, giving you rain from heaven and seasons of bearing fruit, filling your hearts with food and gladness."
And when they had said this, they barely restrained the crowd from sacrificing to them, and instead made them go each to his own home.

And while they were still staying there and teaching, the Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium and spoke to them openly, and turned the crowd to separate from them. They said that they spoke nothing true but lied in everything. And they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, thinking that he was dead.
When the disciples came around to the assembly, he rose up and went into the city, and on the next day he went out with Barnabas and they went to Derbe.
And they preached the gospel to that city and made many disciples, and returned to Lystra, to Iconium and to Antioch,
and they strengthened the hearts of the disciples and exhorted them to remain firm in the faith, saying: "Through many tribulations we must enter the kingdom of God."
And by the laying on of hands they ordained elders for them in each church; with prayer and fasting they commended them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
And when they had passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
And when they had spoken the word of God in Perga, they set out from there and came to Italy [?].
And from there they set out by ship and came to Antioch, from where they had been commended and strengthened by the grace of God for the work which they had accomplished.
And when they had come there, they gathered the congregation and recounted to them all that God had done with them, and that he had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.
And they stayed there no little time with the disciples.
And some came down from Judea and taught the brethren, saying: "Unless you are circumcised according to the law of Moses, you cannot be saved."

When there was no small dissension and disputation between Paul and Barnabas and them, it was then arranged that Paul and Barnabas and some others of them should go up to Jerusalem, to the apostles and elders, about this dispute.

They were sent on their way by the congregation, and they passed through the coastal region and Samaria, recounting to them the conversion of the Gentiles, and they brought great joy to all the brethren.
And when they came and arrived at Jerusalem, the congregation, the apostles and the elders welcomed them, and they told them all that God had done with them.
But some from the party of the Pharisees who had become believers stood up and began to speak, and they said: "They must be circumcised and commanded to keep the law of Moses."
The apostles and the elders gathered to look into this matter and discuss it.

And after there had been much debate, Peter stood up and said to them: "Men, brothers, you yourselves know that from the first days God made it known among you that the Gentiles would hear the word of the gospel from my mouth and believe.
And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them, for he gave them the Holy Spirit just as he gave it to us.
And he made no distinction between us and them; he cleansed their hearts by faith.
Now why are you testing God by putting a yoke on the neck of the disciples that neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
Rather, we believe that we will be saved through the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, in the same way as they."
And the whole crowd fell silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul as they told of all the signs and wonders that God had done among the Gentiles through their hands.
And after they had fallen silent, James answered and said: "Men, brothers, listen to me:
Simeon has told you how God looked upon the Gentiles to take from among them a people for his name;
and the words of the prophets agree with this, as it is written:
'After this I will return and rebuild the dwelling of David; I will raise up what of it has fallen and been overthrown, and I will rebuild it,
so that the rest of humankind may seek the Lord, and all the Gentiles over whom this name of mine is called, says the Lord, who has made
all these things known from eternity.'
Therefore my judgement is this: that we should not trouble those from among the Gentiles who have turned to God,
but should write to them that they abstain, for the time being, from things sacrificed to idols, from fornication, from what is strangled, and from blood;
for from the earliest generations Moses has had his preachers set up in city after city, who read him aloud in the synagogues every sabbath."

Then the apostles and the elders, together with the whole congregation, decided to choose men from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas: Judas, who was called Barsabbas, and Silas, men held in high regard among the brothers.
They wrote a letter by their hand as follows: "The apostles and the elders and the brothers, to the brothers from among the Gentiles who are in Antioch, Syria and the region of Cilicia: greetings.

For we have heard that some from among us went out and stirred you up with words, unsettling [?] your hearts and telling you: 'Circumcision is necessary, and keeping the law of Moses,' though they had no such command from us.
Now therefore it seemed good to us, all the congregations together, to choose these men and send them to you with Paul and Barnabas, our beloved,
men who have given up their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
So we have sent Judas and Silas, and they will also tell you these things by word of mouth,
For it seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us also that no greater burden be laid upon you than these things, which are the most needful:
that you keep away from things sacrificed to idols and from what is dead, and from eating blood, and from fornication. Keep yourselves from these things, do good, and live by the Lord."
When they had been sent on their way, they came to Antioch. There they gathered the congregation together and put the letter into their hands.
When they had read the letter, they rejoiced greatly and were comforted by it.
Judas and Silas, who were also prophets themselves, comforted the brothers with many words and strengthened them.
They spent a long time there. Then the brothers there sent them back in peace to the apostles.
But Silas decided to remain there.
Paul and Barnabas stayed in Antioch. Together with many others, they taught and preached the words of the Lord.
Some days later Paul said to Barnabas: "Let us go back and visit the brothers in every city where we preached the word of the Lord, and see how they are."
Barnabas wanted to take with them John, who was called Mark.
But Paul insisted that they should not take him, since he had separated from them the first time, in Pamphylia, and had not followed them in that work.
So there was a sharp disagreement between them, so sharp that they parted from one another. Barnabas took Mark with him and sailed away by ship to Cyprus.
But Paul chose Silas and set out, after the brothers had commended him to the grace of God.
He passed through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
He arrived at Derbe and Lystra. And there was a certain disciple there named Timothy. He was the son of a believing Jewish woman, and his father was a Gentile.
The brothers of Lystra and Iconium spoke well of him.
Paul wanted him to go out with him, so he took him and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was a Gentile.
As they went through the cities, they taught them to keep the law that had been confirmed by the apostles and elders in Jerusalem.
So the churches were strengthened in the faith and grew in number from day to day.
They went through Phrygia and the region of the Galatians, and the Holy Spirit prevented them from speaking the word in the region of Asia.
When they came to Mysia, they tried to go toward Bithynia, but the Spirit of the Lord did not allow them.
So they passed by Mysia and went down to Troas.
In a vision during the night Paul saw a Macedonian man standing and pleading with him: "Come over to Macedonia and help us."
When Paul had seen this vision, we immediately made haste to set out for Macedonia. We understood that God had called us there to preach the gospel to them.
We boarded a ship at Troas and sailed straight to Samothrace, and on the next day to Neapolis,
by way of Philippi, which is the first part of Macedonia, a city which is called a colony. We were in that city and stayed there some days.
On the Sabbath day we went outside the city to the bank of the river, where it was thought that prayer was offered; and we sat down and spoke to the women who had gathered.
And there was a woman there named Lydia, a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira, a worshipper of God. She was listening, and the Lord opened her heart to heed the words spoken by Paul.
And when she and her household had been baptized, she entreated us and said: "If you have judged me to be a believer in the Lord, come into my house and stay there." And she pressed us.
And as we were going to worship, a slave girl met us who had a spirit of Python, that is, of divination, and through her divination she brought much gain [?] to her masters.
She followed Paul and us, crying out and saying: "These men are servants of the Most High God, who proclaim to you the ways of life."

She did this for many days. Paul grew angry, turned to the evil spirit and said: "I command you in the name of the Lord Jesus Christ to come out of her." And it came out of her immediately, at that very hour.
When the woman's masters saw that the [?] of their gain had gone out of her, they seized Paul and Silas and dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers,
and they brought them and set them before the magistrates, and said: "These men are stirring up this city of ours. They are Jews,
and they proclaim to us a certain law which it is not lawful for us to accept or to practice, for we are Romans."
And the crowd gathered against them, and the magistrates tore off their clothes and ordered them to be beaten with rods.
And when they had laid many blows on them, they threw them into prison and ordered the jailer to guard them carefully.
When he received this order from them, he put them into the inner prison and fastened their feet in the stocks.
About midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the other prisoners were listening to them.
Suddenly there was a great earthquake, and the prison was shaken to its foundations, and at once all the doors were opened and everyone's bonds were loosed.
And when the jailer suddenly woke up and saw the prison doors open, he drew his sword and was about to kill himself, for he thought that all the prisoners had fled.
Paul called to him with a loud voice and said: "Do yourself no harm; we are all here."
He asked for a light and went in, and trembling seized him, and he fell down at the knees of Paul and Silas.
He brought them outside and said: "Sirs, what must I do to be saved?"
They said to him: "Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and you will be saved, you and all your house."
And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, and he believed, together with all his household.
And that same night the chief jailer took them and washed their wounds from the beating, and he himself was baptized, and all his household with him.
And he brought the apostles up, sat them down in his house, and set a table for them. And he rejoiced with all his household, who had believed in the Lord.
And when day dawned, the magistrates sent the officers to him and said, "Release those men whom we handed over to you as prisoners."
The jailer went in and told these words to Paul and Silas, and said to them, "The magistrates have ordered your release. Now go in peace."

Paul said to him, "They beat us in public, men who are innocent and blameless, Roman men, and threw us into prison for nothing. And now they have sent to release us secretly? It is not so. Rather, let them come and bring us out of here themselves."
The officers went and told all this to the magistrates. When they heard it, they were seized with fear, all the more because they heard that the men were Romans.
They came quickly, brought them out of the prison, and begged them to leave and go away from their city.
When they came out of the prison, they went into the house of Lydia. There they saw the brothers, comforted them, and departed.
And when they had passed through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
And as was Paul's custom, he went in to them, and on three Sabbaths he discussed readings from the scriptures with them,
explaining and setting before them that the Christ had to suffer and rise from the dead, and saying, "This is the Christ whom I proclaim to you."
And some of them believed and joined Paul and Silas, as did a great multitude of God-fearing Gentiles and many women of no small standing.

But the Jews became jealous. They brought some wicked men from the marketplace, gathered a crowd, and threw the city into an uproar. They attacked the house of Jason, seeking to bring them out before the people.
And when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and some other brothers before the city rulers, shouting, "These men who have stirred up the whole world have come here too,
and Jason has welcomed them. And all of these act against the decrees of Caesar, saying that there is another king, Jesus."
And with these words they stirred up the people and the city magistrates,
until they took a security from Jason, and only then did they let them go.
When the brothers came, they immediately brought Paul and Silas out that same night and sent them off toward Berea. When they came to that city, they went straight to the synagogue of the Jews.
For these were nobler than those of Thessalonica. They received their word with all eagerness and examined the scriptures continually to see whether these things were so.
Many of them believed, and also some of the Gentiles, including many women and not a few men.
When the Jews of Thessalonica learned that the word of God had been proclaimed by Paul in Berea too, they came there as well and began to stir up the people.
The brothers immediately brought Paul out and sent him off toward the seacoast. Silas and Timothy stayed there.
Those who were escorting Paul brought him as far as Athens. They received a command from Paul for Silas and Timothy to come to him quickly, and they departed.
While he was waiting in the city of Athens, his spirit was provoked within him as he saw that the city was full of idol worship.
He was speaking constantly in the synagogue among the Jews and those who worshipped [God], and in the marketplaces every day with those who happened to meet him.

Some of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers argued with him, and some said: "What does this seed-babbler want to say?" For they said: "This man seems [?] to be a proclaimer of foreign demons," because he was preaching to them the resurrection of Jesus.
They took hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus and said: "May we know what this new teaching of yours is?
You bring some strange things to our ears. We wish to know what these things mean."
Now all the Athenians and the foreigners who had come there spent their time in nothing else but telling and hearing something newer.
Then Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and said: "Men of Athens, I see that in all things you are exceedingly devoted to demons.
For as I was going about and looking at the objects of your worship, I found an altar on which was written: 'Unknown God.' What you do not know and yet worship, this I proclaim to you.
God, who made the world and everything that is in it, he who is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands,
nor is he served by human hands, as though he were in need of anything, for it is he who gives to all life and breath. And
he made from one blood all the races of men to dwell on the whole face of the earth, and he determined the appointed times and the fixed boundaries of their dwelling,
so that they would seek God, if perhaps someone might seek him and find him; and indeed he is not far from each one of us,
for through him we live, as some of your own poets say: 'For we are also his offspring.'
